title: Measurement and Geometry - Lesson 9 Practice: Rectangular Pyramid Volume
description: Practice calculating and estimating rectangular pyramid volumes with correct cubic units.

questions.question: Which formula finds the volume of a rectangular pyramid with length l, width w, and height h?
questions.explanation: A rectangular pyramid has one-third the volume of a rectangular prism with the same base and height, so V = (1/3)lwh.

questions.question: A rectangular pyramid has length 9 cm, width 4 cm, and height 6 cm. What is its volume?
A rectangular pyramid has l = 12 m, w = 5 m, and h = 3 m. Find the volume in m^3. Enter just the number.
The height used in V = (1/3)lwh is the perpendicular distance from the base to the vertex, not a slanted edge.
questions.explanation: Pyramid volume uses the perpendicular height. A slanted edge is not the same measurement.

questions.question: Estimate the volume of a rectangular pyramid with dimensions 7.9 cm, 6.2 cm, and 3.1 cm by rounding to 8 cm, 6 cm, and 3 cm.
questions.explanation: Use V = (1/3)(8)(6)(3). The product is 144, and 144 / 3 = 48 cm^3.

questions.question: A rectangular pyramid has a base area of 42 in^2 and a height of 9 in. What is its volume?
A model tent is a rectangular pyramid with length 6 m, width 4 m, and height 2.5 m. Find its volume in m^3. Enter just the number.
A student calculates (10)(8)(6) = 480 and says the pyramid volume is 480 cm^3. Explain the mistake and give the correct volume.
questions.correctAnswer: The student found the volume of the rectangular prism with the same dimensions but forgot to divide by 3. The correct pyramid volume is 480 / 3 = 160 cm^3.
questions.explanation: A rectangular pyramid is one-third of the matching rectangular prism, so the final step is dividing lwh by 3.
